usage: 辛苦得來 is used to describe something that has been gained or achieved through a lot of effort.
It emphasizes that the result, money, opportunity, or success did not come easily.
It is more common in relatively formal or reflective speech and writing than in very casual everyday Cantonese.
It is often used before nouns, for example: 辛苦得來嘅成果 (hard-earned results) or 辛苦得來嘅機會 (hard-earned opportunity).
In casual spoken Cantonese, people may also use expressions such as 辛苦搵返嚟 or 靠努力得返嚟 depending on the context.

examples.sentence: 呢個機會係我辛苦得來嘅，我一定會珍惜。
examples.jyutping: ni1 go3 gei1 wui6 hai6 ngo5 san1 fu2 dak1 loi4 ge3, ngo5 jat1 ding6 wui5 zan1 sik1.
examples.meaning: This opportunity is hard-earned for me, and I will definitely cherish it.

examples.sentence: 你嘅成績係辛苦得來嘅，唔好輕易放棄。
examples.jyutping: nei5 ge3 sing4 zik1 hai6 san1 fu2 dak1 loi4 ge3, m4 hou2 hing1 ji6 fong3 hei3.
examples.meaning: Your results are hard-earned, so don't give up easily.

examples.sentence: 呢啲錢係我辛苦得來嘅，唔可以亂用。
examples.jyutping: ni1 di1 cin2 hai6 ngo5 san1 fu2 dak1 loi4 ge3, m4 ho2 ji5 lyun6 jung6.
examples.meaning: This money is hard-earned, so it shouldn't be spent carelessly.

examples.sentence: 成功唔容易，辛苦得來先更加有價值。
examples.jyutping: sing4 gung1 m4 jung4 ji6, san1 fu2 dak1 loi4 sin1 gang3 gaa1 jau5 gaa3 zik6.
examples.meaning: Success doesn't come easily; it has even more value when it is hard-earned.

related: 辛苦 (san1 fu2) - hardship; hard work
付出 (fu6 ceot1) - put in; make an effort
